# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# Lines are shown most-fundamental first; the first line doubles as the "foothold".
How do you tell whether one byte of s1 belongs to set, and which bytes of s1 does "removed from the beginning and the end" (p.11) reach?
What if only one end of s1 has bytes of set, or a byte of set sits between two that are not?
What is left when set is empty or matches nothing, and what is left when every byte of s1 is in set? Is there still a string to return?
Is a tab, a line break or a byte above 0x7f anything other than one more byte to compare? Where could a char's sign change a comparison?
Nothing in the subject bounds s1 or set. Does anything in your function stop working once either passes a few thousand bytes?
